articles.title_zh: Pope Leo urges concessions for peace as Ukraine war drags on
articles.content_orig:
France may have a highly secularized culture, but it has given Pope Leo XIV a superstar welcome.
In Paris, around 800,000 lined the Champs-Élysées avenue, some waving Vatican or French flags while others climbed trees or stood on each other’s shoulders to get a glimpse of the popemobile. In Lourdes, a holy site in southern France, around 150,000 attended an open-air papal Mass, according to Vatican estimates which dwarf the numbers of faithful who turned out for the last papal visit in 2008.
During the four-day visit, Leo appeared comfortable and relaxed, delivering most of his speeches and reflections in French, as the Chicago-born pontiff sought to tackle several themes during the trip.
A strong focus of Leo’s has been on trying to revitalize faith in a traditional European Catholic heartland as well as on addressing the clerical sexual abuse scandal and big political topics such as artificial intelligence. He’s also offered some more personal, unscripted remarks, helping to shape a clearer picture of himself.
While his predecessor never made official visits to the major Catholic European countries of France and Spain, Pope Leo has traveled to both within the first year and a half since his election.
France is sometimes described as the “eldest daughter of the church” because of its deep Catholic roots, but it’s also faced a long-term trend of declining church attendance with estimates of just 5-8% of the population heading to the pews each week.
French bishops have more recently reported some good news though: a surprising rise in new church entrants after around 8,200 adolescents and 13,200 adults were baptized in 2026. That’s a 20% increase on the year prior, with the church also saying 42% of the adults seeking baptism are aged 18-25, a reflection of a trend showing Gen Z’s openness to religious faith .
It’s something Pope Leo will have noted at the Stade de France when 80,000 young people packed the venue for a jubilant – and loud – prayer vigil. It was similar to when the pontiff visited Spain in June.
“There is a quest for meaning. People need and are in search of meaning and answers to the big existential question,” Rev. Benoît Pouzin, a priest in southwest France involved in youth ministry, told CNN.
France has a strict separation between church and state, so each papal visit needs to be carefully navigated. But in a surprising twist, Leo’s Mass in Paris was celebrated on the Place de la Concorde, a site deeply linked to the secular Republic as it’s where the last king of France, Louis XVI and Marie-Antoinette were guillotined. The separation of the church started with the fall of the monarchy during the French Revolution.
In another unusual move later in the trip, President Emmanuel Macron also attended a papal Mass in Metz, a city in the northeast, despite criticism in 2023 for doing the same during Pope Francis’ visit.
Many among the crowds also pointed to Leo’s role as the other major US leader on the world stage. It’s hard not to see him as a counterweight to President Donald Trump. In contrast to the Trump administration, the pope has called for stronger guardrails around the development of artificial intelligence, warning against a “paradise of machines” while in Paris.
Pope Leo said he is taking the warnings about Artificial Intelligence’s threat to humanity seriously, and said it is irresponsible for people to sit back and dismiss the risks of AI.
Trump has dismissed the warnings about AI as a “hoax” which he made during a surprise phone call with Jensen Huang, the CEO of chipmaker Nvidia, at a summit in Los Angeles.
“I don’t think that that is fake news – as some have said – to try and pause,” Leo XIV said on board the papal plane from Metz to Rome.
Leo, who has expressed a keen interest in artificial intelligence since the start of his papacy, said that he found it “interesting” that Huang had unveiled a new tool to prevent AI agents from operating out of human control.
“He’s the same one, however, that says there should be no limits placed and no government regulation,” the Pope said.
The pope devoted his first major theological document to AI earlier this year, warning about the use of AI in warfare and calling for stronger ethical foundation to the development of the technology.
The pope explained that the Vatican had established its own AI commission to understand how to use it, along with the risks and benefits, and that “we need to continue to invite political leaders, the leaders of AI” so they can “look at what is happening already and what could be down the road.”
He explained: “We are trying to continue to promote dialog, study, investigation, to find ways to make sure that AI does not get to a point where it could destroy humanity.”
“If someone were to ask me, am I in panic mode? No, I’m not, I sleep at night” the pope said, but added: “I do think that the concerns raised by many of the experts, specialists in AI, should be taken seriously.”
“To simply say, oh, it’s not going to happen and close our eyes to it, I think, is probably not the most responsible way to go about that,” Leo said.
The pope, who spoke out against the US war in Iran, also wants a more united Europe, a stronger European Union and stronger international cooperation. “Today, relations between individuals and states are becoming increasingly uncivilized,” the pope said in Metz on Monday. “The value of keeping one’s word is dismissed; instead, people boast of lies and deceit.”
The pope’s speech also praised one of the founders of the European Union, Robert Schuman, for whom there is an ongoing formal cause to make a saint.
Pope Leo XIV has warned against the use of Christianity by far-right political groups, while calling on the church to be active in seeking to prevent extremism. Speaking on board the papal plane, he said that “the combination of these far-right points of view with a certain kind of religion” cannot be considered an “authentic expression of Christianity.”
The pope’s comments came in response to a question about the rise of extremist parties in Germany as he flew back from making a major speech on European Unity at the French-German border.
“We go back to the values of the Gospel [Christian teaching], which are not about hatred and division, but they’re about understanding and compassion,” the pope said.
The American pontiff also responded to Trump’s White House media ban, which includes CNN and other outlets. In answer to a question from CNN, he said he was “very happy that, here, you are all welcome and good coverage, I think, is very important and that we have it all the way around, for everyone.” The response was classic Leo: signaling his support for the press but not wishing to create an unnecessary dispute with the president.
The American pope’s in-flight interactions with journalists were rare, unscripted moments, with his answers often revealing more about his personality. On the flight from Rome to Paris, the pope was asked if he had anything to do with a miraculous recent Chicago White Sox victory, his beloved baseball team. “No comment,” he said before adding with a smile, “Great things happen in Chicago.”
He also recalled childhood memories of watching Fulton Sheen, the American archbishop and broadcaster who was recently declared “blessed,” one step ahead of sainthood, and revealed he’d been practicing his French but was no longer using the Duolingo language app. “It’s fake news!” he said about recent reports. Leo has in the past been spotted using Duolingo to learn German.
Leo isn’t simply vocal about challenges of his homeland. He also voiced concern over assisted dying with France recently approving legislation granting the right to the incurably ill, which is strongly opposed by the Catholic Church. Leo spoke on the subject several times during his visit – most clearly in the “miracle shrine” town of Lourdes, known for drawing many sick and terminally ill pilgrims to its shrine.

articles.title_orig: Trump and Johnson to meet with tech CEOs on AI risk
articles.title_zh: Trump and Johnson to meet with tech CEOs on AI risk
articles.content_orig:
Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei and Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg are among the tech executives expected at a Tuesday luncheon with President Donald Trump and House Speaker Mike Johnson, CNBC confirmed, according to multiple people familiar with the plans, who spoke on condition of anonymity because the details are not public.
Alphabet CEO Sundar Pichai will also be at the lunch, the company confirmed Monday, as well as Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, according to MS Now. OpenAI President Greg Brockman will be in attendance as well, Reuters reported, citing a person familiar with the matter.
Trump, Vice President JD Vance and other administration officials are hosting an all-day event on Tuesday to announce a new website for federal information and resources, according to a White House official. That event will have panel discussions on artificial intelligence , energy, space and other topics.
Anthropic co-founder and Chief Compute Officer Tom Brown will also be in attendance at the event, according to a person familiar with the plans, who spoke on condition of anonymity because the details are not public.
Last week, multiple big tech executives attended the state dinner for the visit of Chinese President Xi Jinping, including Apple's Tim Cook, SpaceX's Elon Musk and Advanced Micro Devices CEO Lisa Su.
Amodei, who was notably absent from Thursday's China state dinner, had a private dinner with the president on Sunday. It was the first one-on-one meeting between the two leaders, according to a person familiar with the visit, who asked not to be named in order to discuss a confidential matter.
Tuesday's meeting could serve as another opportunity for tech leaders, particularly Amodei, to ease tensions with the White House as the debate over AI safety has spread and leaders have taken sides on potential regulation. A former Anthropic researcher triggered the outcry after he accused AI frontier labs of "gambling with our lives."
Industry leaders like OpenAI chief Sam Altman and Musk have agreed with calls for an industry-wide slowdown, after Amodei penned an essay calling for companies to "pace the frontier" with advanced AI. Trump, on the other hand, has been openly resistant, and in recent weeks called AI fears a "hoax" and a "scam."
CNBC's Ashley Capoot, Julia Boorstin and Mary Catherine Wellons contributed to this report.

articles.title_orig: What We Know About the Arrests at the U.K. Air Base Used by the U.S.
articles.title_zh: What We Know About the Arrests at the U.K. Air Base Used by the U.S.
articles.content_orig:
Five men who were arrested on suspicion of terrorism offences near RAF Fairford are being released on police bail, counter-terror police have said.
A major incident was declared and dozens of homes were evacuated after police were alerted to three "suspicious vehicles" near the airbase in Gloucestershire in the early hours of Sunday morning.
Counter Terrorism Policing (CTP) said officers were exploring "multiple lines of inquiry", including whether proxies or individuals working on behalf of a foreign state were involved.
The five men are all UK nationals in their 20s from London.
They were initially detained on suspicion of committing offences under the Explosives Act and then further arrested on suspicion of preparation of a terrorist act.
Counter-terror police said they remained under investigation and their release was "subject to stringent conditions on their movement and contact with others".
Three of the men live in Westminster, one in Camden and another in Willesden, police said, and they are aged between 23 and 25.
A farmer who called 999 to report the three white vans in the village of Whelford, which lies directly east of the base, told the BBC it was "pure luck" that she spotted them.
The woman, who wished to remain anonymous, said she arrived home to find the driveway and road blocked and saw a "large group of hooded and masked men".
"When they saw me they ran ahead of me - some into the field and some towards the neighbouring village of Kempsford. I then realised that something highly unusual was taking place," she told BBC Radio 4's Today programme.
She said that she called the Ministry of Defence police at RAF Fairford but received no answer. She then rang 999 at 01:36 BST and said "within 10 minutes the village was full of armed police".
"I believe that my 999 call foiled whatever plans they had," she added.
Assistant Commissioner Laurence Taylor, head of Counter Terrorism Policing, said on Monday afternoon that the three "suspicious vehicles" had been "subject to extensive examination, with the support of military assets and forensic experts".
Officers were considering the incident "from every possible angle", including that "this may be activity committed by proxies, or individuals either knowingly or unknowingly, working on behalf of a foreign state", he added.
Prime Minister Andy Burnham chaired a Cobra meeting on Monday afternoon and urged people "not to speculate while the authorities establish the full facts".
The Iranian embassy in London said it "categorically rejects and strongly condemns" what it called "unfounded and malicious speculations" linking Iran to the incident, adding that these would "serve no purpose other than to fuel Iranophobia propaganda in the UK".
The embassy said Iran "reserves the right to take appropriate legal measures, as necessary, to safeguard the rights and interests of the country and its people in response to misleading and damaging media narratives".
The RAF base has been used as a forward operating location by the US Air Force (USAF) for decades.
In recent months, US bombers have taken off from the base for the Middle East, after the UK approved a US request to use it for defensive strikes on Iran.
In July, Iran said "any base used for aggression against Iranian territory constitutes a legitimate target for our forces".
Speaking at the Oval Office on Monday, US President Donald Trump said he wouldn't have let the five men arrested out on bail, and that he was "surprised" they had been released.
"We know everything about them, we would not have released them," he said, adding that the UK had worked with the US "very closely" on this.
A large cordon remains in place near the base, while 85 households who were evacuated on Sunday have now been told by Gloucestershire Police that they can return home.
But police have said a cordon will remain around the three vehicles.
Gloucestershire Constabulary's Temporary Chief Constable Maggie Blyth said the last 48 hours had thrown "our usually quiet and peaceful communities under the spotlight of the international media".
Airspace restrictions have also been put in place above the base - nobody can fly within a five mile (8km) zone encircling it without permission. Banned items include balloons, kites, parachutes and paragliders.

articles.title_orig: Sixers’ LeBron James, ‘living in the moment,’ squashes retirement talk
articles.title_zh: Sixers’ LeBron James, ‘living in the moment,’ squashes retirement talk
articles.content_orig:
A little after noon on a dreary Monday morning, kids wearing school uniforms spilled onto the playground in downtown Camden.
It was recess at LEAP Academy, and the kids milled about the macadam or waited their turn on the swings, contentedly unaware that, just a few blocks away, the King had just arrived to claim his new kingdom.
At around 11:15 a.m. ET, LeBron James followed a phalanx of front office and public relations staff into a second-floor room, sat down behind a table draped in blue cloth and promptly began clearing the table. He took a water bottle meant for his sipping and plopped it on the floor, yanked a microphone off its stand and finally glanced at a placard with his name.
“You guys know who I am, right?” he said, before putting the name card on the floor, too.
This, of course, is why James is here, wearing the red, white and blue of the Philadelphia 76ers: To rearrange things. To bring structure and order to a franchise that has been mired in mediocrity.
And, if all goes as he plans, to upend the NBA pecking order.
“I didn’t leave my family,” he said of his relocation to Philly while his family stays encamped out west, “to lose in the second round.”
Had the Liberty Bell still been able, it might have peeled off in glee at that moment.
In his first official duty as a 76er, James hit all the proper notes. He spoke graciously for nearly 20 minutes, waxing thoughtfully about the difficulty of juggling parenthood with superstardom, and sharing honestly his reasoning behind joining the Sixers. He invoked the Palestra (he played there as a high schooler) and paid proper homage to the demanding fan base (“We respect you, but we hate you. I love that,” he said).
But it is those 11 words that Philly fans, who are at 25 years and counting without so much as a berth in the Eastern Conference Finals, will devour. The question, of course, is whether they will be on James’ statue or carved into his gravestone.
Declarations here – of independence and otherwise – have a way of hanging around. The same people who embraced Moses Malone’s prediction of “Fo Fo Fo,” about the Sixers’ 1983 NBA title run (it wound up Fo, Fi, Fo) also remember that, 31 years ago, Ricky Watters replied, “For who? For what?” when asked why he didn’t lay out for a throw from quarterback Randall Cunningham.
“They know sports. They know ball,” James said of his new fan base. “But if you’re not doing what you’re supposed to do, they’re going to let you hear it. They’re going to hold you accountable.”
The worry about what will come, though, is for another day. For once, the September Sixers offered excitement about what could be.
Ordinarily the Sixers’ media day would have fallen largely on deaf ears, a speed bump on a calendar filled with far more important dates. Nine hours after the Sixers commenced their interviews, the undefeated Eagles would play the Bears on “Monday Night Football.” On Tuesday, when training camp officially begins in Camden, the Phillies begin their quest for “Red October,” after belatedly securing a wildcard slot in the eleventh hour.
But this Saturday, the Sixers will play their Blue x White scrimmage in the downtown arena for the first time, to allow for more fans, and the get-in price for the home opener is already pushing toward $300. Actual media day, usually reserved for a few ink-stained regulars, was near standing-room only, with one team official bemoaning a Phoebe Bridgers concert that prevented the team from moving the event to the team’s home arena in Philadelphia.
This is what hope looks like, what it feels like when a franchise actually has a plan and not just a process. General manager Mike Gansey pulled off the coups of the offseason, not just signing James but securing Jaylen Brown in a trade with the Celtics that was as brazen as it was stealthy.
“If it had leaked,” executive vice president for basketball operations Jameer Nelson told CNN Sports. “I’m not sure it happens. That’s just my opinion.”
Brown’s arrival started the ball rolling. Tyrese Maxey sealed the deal. The precocious 25-year-old became a workout pal with James post-Covid 19 pandemic, the two bonding on their insatiable desire to do the work. In the offseasons since the pandemic, they became regular partners, both hitting 6 a.m. workouts together. Clearly impressed with Maxey’s dedication and pluck, James asked him for an honest evaluation of the Sixers.
Still – even though Philly was on James’ agent’s famed whiteboard of destinations – it seemed like a long shot even to those involved.
VJ Edgecombe was getting a pedicure when he heard about his new teammate and Nelson was at an AirBnB in Huntington Beach, California, for his daughter’s softball tournament when the news became official. Unable to tell his family, Nelson played dumb until Jayce started screaming, “LeBron is coming to Philly!”
Once the deal was done, Edgecombe set about creating a new team text chain.
“But I don’t have LeBron’s number,” he said with a grin. “And even I did, I wasn’t adding him to it. I made Tyrese do that.”
Even those on the text chain admit they’re still a little starry eyed. James officially became a Sixer on July 27, but this is his first time in Philly (that he arrived on the heels of a Nor’easter reminded him of what he’s in for with the East Coast weather).
“I thought I was over it,” Jabari Walker said. “But then it was like, ‘Wait. He’s in the locker room now.’”
On Tuesday, James will be on the practice court. That is, frankly, where he plans to do his best work. He can still play – “the luxury of my game is I can do everything,” he quipped. “Literally I can do everything” – but he thrives in creating an incubator for success. He threw shade at unnamed players who averaged big numbers in their careers, but secured no postseason success, and pooh-poohed an “instant oatmeal” society that wants everything handed out easily.
James loves, at the risk of using a word that will make Philly fans flinch, “the process,” but his comes with four championship rings on his fingers.
“You have to fall in love with doing things that are uncomfortable,” he said. “And if we can do that, we can be a great team. If we don’t do that, then we’ll be like, ‘Oh man. That was a great team on paper and we had a lot of great talent, and we lost in the second round.’”

Hello football friends, and welcome to the Monday edition of the Pick Six newsletter!
If you're still trying to recover from Sunday's NFL action, welcome to the club. Every time I thought Week 3 couldn't get any crazier, it somehow got crazier. In the early slate of games, we saw the Commanders -- who just LOST their starting quarterback last week -- take down the undefeated Super Bowl champion Seahawks 33-31.
That was one of seven upsets that we saw in Week 3.
If you felt like every game on Sunday was close, you're not crazy. There were a total of 12 games decided by a single possession, which is tied for the most for any day in NFL history and the most for any week in league history. If we get a one-score game tonight, that will set the NFL record for most one-score games in a week, but don't count on that happening, because every Monday night game has been a blowout so far.

As always, here's your daily reminder to tell all your friends to sign up for the newsletter. To get them signed up, just click here .

Statement: The Raiders are going to make the playoffs. Overreaction or reality: Overreaction. The Raiders can only play who is on their schedule, and their wins are now over the Chargers (who look miserable), the Dolphins (who might not win a game) and the Saints (who might be good but might be just OK).  Let me be perfectly clear: It's OK if the Raiders aren't going to make the playoffs. They already have as many wins this year as they did last year. Kubiak has done wonderful stuff, the young players look great, the free agent additions look great, and it's already one of the most impressive turnarounds of the year.

The difficulty level on some of his throws is really impressive. Lawrence is simply playing at an extremely high level. He wasn't great last week at the Broncos , but as we've already seen, every quarterback has off weeks. He is finally unlocking everything we projected he could be when he was coming out of Clemson: big arm that can access the entire field, impressive athleticism and awesome downfield accuracy, especially over the middle of the field.
Statement: Brock Purdy is playing as well as he ever has. Overreaction or reality: Reality. Let's give Brock Purdy his due. This season, he ranks: 1st in net yards per attempt (9.5), 1st in EPA per dropback (0.62), 1st in success rate (65.6%), 1st in touchdown rate (10.8%), 3rd in completion percentage (72.3%). Now, Kyle Shanahan always has uber-efficient offenses. He's also doing this with no Ricky Pearsall , no De'Zhaun Stribling and no DeMarcus Robinson . Mike Evans left Sunday's game, too.

After Jaxson Dart got injured last week, John Harbaugh made it clear that the Giants were going to add a quarterback and that's exactly what they did on Monday by acquiring J.J. McCarthy from the Vikings.
Here are the trade details:
This seems like a win-win for both sides. The Vikings were definitely out on McCarthy. After he lost the team's QB battle to Kyler Murray during training camp, it seemed like it was only a matter of time before Minnesota made the decision to move on.
Getting a fifth-round pick in return for a guy who was taken 10th overall isn't ideal, but it's better than nothing. As for the Giants, this a classic Harbaugh move. McCarthy played for Jim Harbaugh at Michigan and you can bet that John gave his brother a call before making the decision to go after McCarthy.
The Giants' offense is at its best when a mobile quarterback is running the show and New York just wasn't going to have that with Jameis Winston under center. With McCarthy getting up to speed, Winston will almost certainly be the starter for New York's Week 4 game against Arizona, but it will be interesting to see what the Giants do after that.

articles.title_orig: Next entry-level Kindle may get rounded screen corners and new colors
articles.title_zh: Next entry-level Kindle may get rounded screen corners and new colors
articles.content_orig:
Amazon may be preparing a new version of its entry-level Kindle. Leaked marketing images show an e-reader that resembles the 2024 model but has flatter edges, rounded display corners and a power button on its right side.
The images, shared by leaker Roland Quandt, show the device in several pastel colors. The Kindle name appears below the screen and on the back, but Amazon’s smile logo is absent from the images.
The power button is another visible change. Rather than sitting on the bottom edge, as it does on the current entry-level Kindle, it appears near the top of the new device’s right-hand side.
The leaked images seem to show two slightly different designs. In some, the screen appears nearly flush with the front of the reader and has a more pronounced border. In others, it looks more recessed. The sample text also differs in size and spacing.
Those differences do not confirm that Amazon intends to release two models. The images could depict separate variants, but they could also show preliminary designs or marketing materials that will change before launch.

As the weekend nor’easter comes to a close, the National Weather Service said lingering rain and wind could cause minor flooding into Monday evening.
According to NWS Meteorologist Bryan Ramsey, New Yorkers should expect light rain Monday but the city will be drying up throughout the week after.
“ We have the system still lingering in the area,” Ramsey said. “It is far weaker than it was before, but you'll continue to see drizzle to light rain chances continue into the day …  Any lingering impacts would be a couple spots where we could see some more minor flood benchmarks being hit for coastal flooding.”
Ramsey said that would align with the Monday morning to afternoon high-tide cycle on the city’s beachfronts.
While New York City experienced high winds and heavy rain over the weekend, the National Weather Service reported a greater concentration of downed trees and structures on Long Island. The agency also said there was moderate to major coastal flooding conditions on Long Island that left two to three feet of inundation in certain areas.
New York City’s Emergency Management Department said the storm brought “widespread” rain, wind gusts of over 50 mph and major levels of floodwater around Jamaica Bay. NYCEM spokesperson Ashleigh Holmes didn’t share any data of the number of homes or infrastructure damaged, but urged New Yorkers to report any damage to the city and file a 311 request for basement flooding, sewer backups, downed trees and other issues.
The season’s first — and early — nor’easter is, however, wrapping up.
“It should just be gradual improvement from here,” Ramsey said.

iPhone Duo is coming October 23 , but there are several unannounced features coming to its StandBy mode that were just discovered hidden in Apple code.
When iPhone Duo arrives next month, it will be the most versatile iPhone yet. That’s in part due to its two displays, but also thanks to special modes that are available in different setups.
You can use iPhone Duo folded or unfolded, in landscape or portrait, and in “seated” or “standing” configurations.
Standing is a great setup for watching videos, but it also enables a range of new StandBy features. And unlike previous iPhones, you can use iPhone Duo’s StandBy mode even when it’s not charging.
Apple showed off several StandBy examples at its unveiling earlier this month. But additional features have just been uncovered by leaker pdfu.
